IS : 10196 - 1982 

Indian Standard 

GUIDELINES FOR 

TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY AND 

CREMATED REMAINS OF HUMAN BEINGS 

BY AIR 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 30 June 1982, after the draft finalized by the Air Cargo Handling 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Move- 
ment and Packaging Division Council. 

0.2 In preparation of this standard provisions of Aircraft ( Public Health ) 
Rules 1954 have also been taken into consideration. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down guidelines for transportation of dead 
body and cremated remains of human beings by air. 

2. REQUIREMENTS 

2.0 General — Dead body or human remains of persons who may have 
died of yellow fever, plague, anthra-gianders or other diseases as specified 
by the Indian Government from time to time shall not be carried except 
for properly cremated ashes. 

2.1 Treatment of Dead Body — Dead body shall be embalmed and 
the embalming shall be guaranteed for six months. 

2.2 Containment of Dead Body — It shall be contained in an inner 
coffin which shall subsequently be put in an outer coffin. The inner 
coffin if intact and free from any offensive odour may be enclosed as 
such in the outer coffin. But if not free from odour its contents shall be 
sealed in a hermetically sealed inner coffin made of lead or zinc. The 
outer coffin shall be stout and shall be made of any hard wood lined 
with zinc or tin and filled with saw dust impregnated with carbolic 
powder. 



IS : 10196 - 1982 

2.3 Handling — Carriage of dead body in coffins on passenger and 
cargo aircraft shall be subject to the following conditions: 

a) Dead body coffin shall not be loaded in the same hold as dogs 
and other sensitive animals. Nor shall it be loaded in the same 
hold as food for human consumption unless such food is packed 
hermetically; and 

b) The pilot in command shall be informed of carriage of dead 
body. 

2.4 Cremated Remains — Cremated remains shall be transported in 
urns which are efficiently cushioned against breakage by suitable packing. 

2.4,1 The handing and loading of urns shall be as normal cargo. 

2.5 Certificate — The body shall be accompained with a certificate 
issued by the Government authority and endorsed by the concerned 
diplomatic representative, in case foreigners. 

2*6 Advance Intimation — The consignee as well as air transport 
service shall inform to the Health Officer of the Airport of arrival an 
advance intimation of at least 24 hours of the importation of the dead 
body or human remains.
